# Claude Code Plugin and Marketplace Format

## Authority tier

Tier A

## Status

foundation

## Owner / maintainer

Anthropic (Claude Code documentation).

## URL

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference
and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces

## Last checked

2026-08-17

## Scope

Authoritative for the on-disk shape of a plugin, the marketplace catalog schema, how a
client resolves a plugin version, and when an installed plugin does or does not receive an
update.

## Why trusted

Official product documentation for the runtime that loads these files. A packaging rule that
contradicts it simply will not install or will not update on a user's machine.

## Caveats

Field sets grow between releases (`defaultEnabled` requires v2.1.154+, `experimental.*` is
explicitly experimental). Verify against the installed CLI (`claude plugin validate <path>`)
rather than assuming a field exists everywhere.

## Extracted rules

### Manifest

- Only `name` is required in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; kebab-case, no spaces.
- `.claude-plugin/` holds **only** `plugin.json`. Every component directory (`skills/`,
  `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/`, `workflows/`, `output-styles/`) lives at the plugin root.
- Manifest paths are relative and start with `./`; `../shared` fails after installation.
- `skills` **extends** the default `skills/` scan; `commands`, `agents`, `workflows`,
  `outputStyles` **replace** the default; `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `lspServers` **merge**.
- A single-skill plugin may keep `SKILL.md` at the root with no `skills/` directory.
- Bundled scripts resolve through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`; state that must survive updates
  goes to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`.

### Version and updates — the part that decides whether fixes ever arrive

- Resolution order: `version` in `plugin.json` → `version` in the marketplace entry → git
  commit SHA (git-hosted sources) → SHA-256 digest (archives) → `unknown`.
- The client **skips the update when the resolved version equals the installed one**.
- Therefore `version` in `plugin.json` **pins** the plugin: pushing new commits without
  bumping that string leaves every existing user on the cached copy.
- Omitting `version` for a git-hosted source falls back to the commit SHA, so users get the
  change on the next marketplace refresh. The documentation calls this the simplest setup
  for internal or actively developed plugins.
- Do not set `version` in both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry: `plugin.json` always
  wins silently, so a stale manifest masks the catalog value.
- Version is the cache key; each version gets its own directory under
  `~/.claude/plugins/cache`, and orphaned versions are pruned after roughly 14 days.

### Marketplace catalog

- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` requires `name` (kebab-case, public-facing) and `owner`.
- Each entry requires `name` and `source`.
- One marketplace per name per user: adding a second with the same name replaces the first,
  so multiple plugins must be listed in one catalog file.
- Users refresh with `/plugin marketplace update` (or `claude plugin marketplace update`);
  a marketplace pinned to a branch or tag `ref` follows that ref, not the default branch.

## Do not use this source for

Deciding what belongs *inside* a skill — content quality, methodology, token budget, or
whether a skill should exist at all. It specifies the container, not the payload.

## Notes

Checked against the installed CLI on 2026-08-17: `claude plugin validate` warns when
`version` is absent. That warning is advisory — for this repository the deliberate choice is
to omit `version` and track commit SHAs, because auto-updating beats a manual bump ritual.
